MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Prenatal diagnostic amniocentesis for maternal cell contamination assessment

CLINICAL INDICATION
Maternal cell contamination testing requested to ensure sample integrity prior to further genetic analysis

TEST PERFORMED
Maternal Cell Contamination Analysis by PCR
Test Code: MCC-PCR-16

METHODOLOGY
Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplification and fragment analysis of 16 highly polymorphic short tandem repeat (STR) loci distributed across chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Maternal blood sample and fetal amniotic fluid sample were analyzed in parallel. Fluorescently labeled PCR products were separated by capillary electrophoresis on an Applied Biosystems 3730xl DNA Analyzer. Data analysis performed using GeneMapper software v5.0. The assay has a sensitivity to detect maternal cell contamination at levels ≥10%.

Loci Analyzed:
Chromosome 13: D13S252, D13S325, D13S634, D13S628
Chromosome 18: D18S976, D18S391, D18S819, D18S535, D18S978, D18S386, D18S390
Chromosome 21: D21S11, D21S1409, D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1446

RESULTS
Maternal Cell Contamination: NOT DETECTED

All 16 polymorphic loci showed distinct fetal allele patterns with no evidence of maternal alleles above background levels. The test excludes maternal cell contamination above the 10% detection threshold.

Quality Metrics:
- All loci successfully amplified in both maternal and fetal samples
- Peak height ratios within expected ranges
- No evidence of allelic dropout
- Positive and negative controls performed as expected

INTERPRETATION
No significant maternal cell contamination was detected in the submitted amniotic fluid sample. The absence of detectable maternal DNA contamination indicates that this sample is suitable for subsequent prenatal genetic testing.

RECOMMENDATIONS
The amniotic fluid sample is appropriate for further genetic analysis. Additional DNA testing is available if clinically indicated, including:
- Chromosomal microarray analysis
- Targeted gene sequencing
- Whole exome sequencing
- Other molecular genetic tests as appropriate

TECHNICAL NOTES
This test is designed to detect maternal cell contamination in prenatal samples. The assay cannot detect contamination below 10% or contamination from sources other than the biological mother. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings and other laboratory data.

LIMITATIONS
- Detection limit: 10% maternal cell contamination
- Does not detect paternal contamination
- Does not detect contamination from other sources
- Rare polymorphisms may affect interpretation

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Clinical Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
